1. Data Controller

The data controller is Luigi Casagrande, reachable at luigi.casagrande@outlook.it

2. Scope of This Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy describes how personal data are processed when users visit the website https://luigicasagrande.it (the “Website”).

The Website is a static, informational website and does not include forms, newsletters, comment sections, or user accounts.

3. Types of Data Processed

3.1 Browsing

During normal operation, the Website and its underlying infrastructure may process the following technical data:

  • IP address
  • browser and device information (User-Agent)
  • date and time of access
  • requested URL

These data are necessary for the delivery and security of the Website and are not used to identify users.

3.2 Voluntary Download

The Website provides access to downloadable documents (e.g. PDF files, CV).
Downloading such files is a voluntary action initiated by the user. No tracking or profiling related to downloads is performed by the Website.

4. Purpose of Processing

Personal data are processed exclusively for the following purposes:

  • ensuring the correct technical functioning of the Website
  • maintaining security and preventing abuse
  • displaying requested content

No data are used for marketing, profiling, or behavioural analysis.

5. Legal Basis of Processing

The processing of personal data is based on the legitimate interest of the data controller pursuant to Article 6(1)(f) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), namely the operation and security of a publicly accessible website.

6. Cookies and Tracking Technologies

The Website does not use cookies, including technical, analytical, or profiling cookies.

The data controller does not intentionally store information on the user’s device (e.g. via cookies, localStorage, or similar technologies).

7. Third-Party Services

7.1 Hosting

The Website is hosted on GitHub Pages.
GitHub may process technical browsing data as a data processor in order to provide the hosting service, in accordance with its own privacy policies.

7.2 DNS Services

Domain name resolution is provided by OVH, which may process technical request data in the context of DNS resolution.

7.3 Google Fonts

The Website uses Google Fonts, loaded from Google servers.
When a page is accessed, the user’s browser may contact Google servers to retrieve font files, which may result in the processing of technical data (such as IP address).

Google acts as an independent data controller for this processing.

7.4 Social Media Links and Widgets

The Website contains links or widgets related to social platforms (e.g. GitHub, LinkedIn).
When interacting with such elements or following external links, users are subject to the privacy policies of the respective third parties.

8. Analytics

The Website does not currently use analytics or traffic measurement tools.

If privacy-friendly, self-hosted analytics solutions (e.g. Umami) are introduced in the future, this Privacy Policy will be updated accordingly.

9. Data Retention

Technical data are retained only for the time strictly necessary to ensure the operation and security of the Website, in accordance with the policies of the involved service providers.

10. Data Transfers Outside the EU

Some third-party services used by the Website (e.g. GitHub, Google) may involve data transfers outside the European Union.
Such transfers are carried out in accordance with applicable data protection regulations and safeguards.

11. Security Measures

Appropriate technical and organizational measures are implemented to protect data against unauthorized access, alteration, or loss.
The Website is served exclusively via HTTPS with a valid TLS certificate.

12. Data Subject Rights

Users may exercise the rights provided by Articles 15–22 of the GDPR, including the right to:

  • access personal data
  • request rectification or erasure
  • object to processing
  • request restriction of processing

Requests may be addressed to the data controller using the contact details provided above.

13. Changes to This Privacy Policy

This Privacy Policy may be updated to reflect changes in the Website, applicable law, or processing activities.
The current version is always available on this page.
title: Privacy Policy

During my exchange period at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, I completed several coursework projects in materials science.
Unlike the lecture notes shown here, these are self-contained studies developed within specific course contexts, specifically with a stronger emphasis on modelling, analysis, or literature review.

The documents below are shared as originally submitted, with only minor adjustments where necessary.

Projects

• Modelling the Melting Behaviour of Pure Ni, Zr, and Ni-Zr Alloys

A molecular dynamics study (LAMMPS) of melting and phase transitions in pure Ni, Zr, and Ni-Zr intermetallics, with focus on atomistic-scale thermal behaviour.

📑 Report

• Understanding Physical Aging and Its Mechanical Characterization

Analysis of physical aging in glassy polymers, focusing on stress relaxation and creep compliance within a viscoelastic framework.

📑 Report 📊 Presentation

• Review: Gum-Based Functional Materials

Literature review on gum-based materials, with emphasis on rheological behaviour and structure–property relationships in soft systems.

📑 Review
title: Academic Projects at SJTU

content:
I started using LaTeX in 2020, right at the beginning of my studies at Politecnico di Milano.
I was first introduced to it by a PhD student who showed a small group of us the basics; nothing too formal, just enough to get started.
That was enough to get me interested, and I ended up picking up the rest on my own.

My workflow started with TeXstudio, but I switched pretty quickly to Visual Studio Code, which I still use now. I rely on a few extensions (LaTeX Workshop, LaTeX language support, and a spell checker) which cover most of what I need without getting in the way.

A big part of how I work is built around custom snippets and commands. I’ve ended up with 150+ of them over time, mostly for things I write all the time: common structures, bits of math, formatting. It saves a lot of repetition, and since I wrote them myself, I don’t have to think twice about how they behave.

At this point LaTeX is basically where all my academic writing happens: lecture notes, reports, everything.
I care about how things read on the page just as much as the content itself, so typesetting isn’t really an afterthought for me.

There’s a more detailed breakdown of the setup here: LaTeX Setup (still missing).

The material presented below is a curated and intentionally reduced selection of notes and projects. Full documents are not publicly distributed; excerpts are shared for documentation purposes only.

Lecture Notes

The following notes were developed during my Master’s studies and are written entirely in LaTeX. They are provided as partial excerpts as explained earlier.

• Failure of Metals

Notes on mechanical failure in metallic systems, covering embrittlement, fracture mechanics, fatigue, creep, and experimental methods. The focus is on interpretation of failure mechanisms and limitations of engineering models.

📑 Failure of Metals

• Materials for Energy

Notes addressing materials challenges in energy applications, structured around degradation mechanisms, high-temperature behaviour, and design constraints in both conventional and renewable systems.

📑 Materials for Energy

• Mathematical Methods

Theoretical notes supporting continuum mechanics and materials modelling, including functional spaces, distributions, Fourier transforms, and partial differential equations.

📑 Mathematical Methods

• Surface Engineering

Notes on surface phenomena and engineering treatments, including friction, lubrication, electroplating (chromium, zinc), and advanced coating technologies.

📑 Surface Engineering

• Metallic Materials and Product Innovation

Notes exploring advanced metallic systems and their role in product development, including shape memory alloys, superconductivity, thermoelectricity, additive manufacturing, and high-entropy alloys.

📑 Metallic Materials and Product Innovation
title: LaTeX Notes for Politecnico di Milano
